title: Fetch the Future
setup: An unmanned human scout enters the district. Fetch assumes it is an invasion probe; the crew needs to identify its function before anyone fires.
escalation: The scout mistakes armed animals for a failed containment event and triggers defensive barriers. Fetch's old command tactics make the situation worse. Ghost tracks its limited sensor pattern while Neon establishes a short diagnostic exchange using the archived protocol.
resolution: The crew disables only the scout's weapon relay and preserves its navigation recorder. Fetch publicly accepts responsibility for escalating the encounter. The recorder supplies a reliable arrival window and confirms a crewed vessel is coming.
continuity: No humans are physically present yet. The scout is a machine with bounded behavior, not proof that all returning people are hostile. Fetch earns cooperation through accountability.
comedy: Fetch delivers a flawless surrender demand to a machine that thinks he wants a walk.
ending_hook: The scout carries an old inventory list describing the entire city as a managed habitat.
status: Development draft — not scripted or recorded
